messages:
support-ops: Heads-up — we just got a Priority 2 from ACME about high p95/p99 on their Dedicated pool (pool-id: dp-east-2). Started ~10:10 UTC, large spike in tail latency, customers seeing 3-6s p95 and 8-12s p99 for small chat requests. Posting initial metrics and repro steps we collected.

maria: thx. do we know whether this is steady or bursty? any autoscaler events? :thinking:

sre-bot: Autoscaler event stream: [2024-06-20T10:08:34Z] scale_out triggered (pool dp-east-2) -> target_replicas 12, current 7. [2024-06-20T10:09:05Z] provisioning start for 5 GPUs. average provisioning lag 38s. [2024-06-20T10:10:12Z] first new node registered. max scale-up lag observed 67s.

ajay: sounds like classic scale-up lag + cold GPU start + saturation. can we see queue length / inflight? any 429s or request timeouts?

support-ops: queue length (requests waiting to be scheduled) peaked at 180 (10:09:30). Inflight tokens per replica ~32. Error rate: 0.6% 500s (model runtime OOM retries), 0.2% 429s. No auth failures. We pushed sample traces to the thread.

kevin: can you paste the repro curl we used for the ACME load test? want to try locally against staging pool.

support-ops: sure — this is the simplified repro that mirrors ACME traffic (short prompts, frequent concurrency):

```
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rw-medium-1","input":"Hi","max_tokens":32}' &
done
wait
```

olivia: ACME says it started after they enabled a scheduled batch of user notifications from 10:00->10:05. traffic jumped 3x for that window.

javier: looked at instance boot logs — long CUDA initialization on a couple of older GPU SKU nodes (p4d-style). Cold-start kernel compilation took ~22-35s, plus container startup 6-10s. combined ~= 40-45s baseline. then runtime warms KV cache (~10-20s depending on session size).

maria: so timeline: spike at 10:08 -> autoscaler triggers -> 30-70s to get GPUs ready -> during that time queue grows -> p95/p99 blow up. we need mitigations: short-term and long-term.

dennis: short-term triage options we can apply now:
- enable burst capacity (if available) to lower scheduling queue
- temporarily route ACME to hosted fallback model (smaller instance) while dedicated pool spins up
- manually bump reserved replicas in dp-east-2 (emergency scale) — javier can we add 3 warm nodes now?

javier: I can spin 3 warm nodes in 90s (manual). note: manual warm nodes can use prebuilt image to skip some compilation but still need kernel JIT for certain ops. I can tag them as warm-pool.

ajay: other quick operational mitigations: reduce concurrency_per_replica for that pool to 16 so each GPU uses lower inflight, which reduces queue head-of-line; reduce model max_seq/default request size for ACME route temporarily; enable fast-fallback routing to quantized model variant rw-medium-1-q4.

maria: agree. let's do a sequence: 1) route ACME to fallback quantized model (ajay) 2) decrease concurrency_per_replica to 16 (config change, kevin) 3) javier to create 3 warm nodes 4) enable autoscaler headroom to keep min_replicas=10 for next 2 hours

ajay: routing change done — ACME traffic routed to rw-medium-1-q4 (transparent for them). expect immediate p95 improvement if the bottleneck was compute. confirm in 30s.

kevin: lowered concurrency flag in pool config and restarted pool controller. new value 16. Watch queue.

sre-bot: Observability: p95 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.1s within 45s of routing change. queue length fell from 180 -> 40. p99 still elevated at ~3.8s.

maria: progress. p99 still high — probably a few cold GPUs serving some sessions with heavy KV cache fills. javier any ETA on warm nodes?

javier: warm nodes starting, one registered (10:10:12), second at 10:10:40, third at 10:11:05. They used prebuilt image and warmed model checkpoints proactively. should cut cold start tail.

support-ops: after warm nodes fully registered, p99 down to ~1.6s and p95 ~0.9s. ACME confirmed latency improved. they've asked for root cause and permanent fixes.

maria: root cause summary (draft): dedicated pool dp-east-2 experienced a sudden 3x traffic increase from scheduled job. Autoscaler correctly triggered scale-out but observed provisioning lag (kernel JIT + cold GPU init + KV population) produced 30-70s scale-up delay. During that window queue backlog caused p95/p99 regressions. Some older GPU SKUs had longer kernel compilation times which amplified tail.

olivia: ACME wants an SLA note and asks if we can avoid this in future (they've paid for reserved capacity but not at the traffic peak). they'd like a mitigation plan.

maria: suggested short-term SLOs for Dedicated customers: reserved headroom option (+X replicas reserved), scheduled pre-warm hooks for predictable jobs (customers can declare scheduled bursts), and platform-level pre-warm for recent/recurrent traffic patterns. long-term: faster cold-start by shipping precompiled kernels with images and maintaining a warm hot-pool replica set across pools.

ajay: notes for engineering: 1) implement container image that includes precompiled kernels for common model families (reduces JIT time) 2) autoscaler change: target add buffer replicas: desired = max(current, ceil(traffic / rp_per_device) + headroom) 3) implement rolling warm pool of minimal-nodes per region that can be snapped into Dedicated pools quickly 4) enable priority-based fallback routing to hosted instances when dedicated backlog exceeds threshold

kevin: also consider reducing inflight default from 32->24 for rw-medium family; we tested 16 and it helped but might reduce throughput for steady workloads — maybe make it per-customer override.

javier: operationally we can also add warm node boots to the provisioning path that skip kernel compile by using a golden image (we need to keep image updated though). cost tradeoff.

dennis: I'll follow up with ACME on timeline & what we changed. we should collect post-mortem details: timestamps, autoscaler logs, node boot logs, model init logs, and customer traffic schedule.

maria: action items:
- dennis: customer comms (ack + what we changed) — due in 30m
- ajay: ticket for precompile kernels + warm pool design doc — PRD by EOD
- javier: propose golden image build steps + rollout plan, include how to refresh kernels safely — due tomorrow
- kevin: proposal for per-customer concurrency defaults & pool-level headroom knobs — due EOD
- maria: draft incident writeup with timeline and dashboards — due by EOD

sre-bot: Incident severity set to Sev2.

olivia: ACME replied: "Thanks — initial perf is good. We appreciate the temporary routing. Can we get scheduled pre-warm API so we can declare our notification windows?"

maria: noted. we should add API for scheduled pre-warm declarations + UI toggle in console that converts to a pre-warm job at ramp times.

ajay: final note — for immediate prevention we should add an autoscaler config flag: min_warm_replicas and kernel_precompile=true. we can flip this on for high-tier Dedicated customers until long-term fixes ship.

kevin: created internal ticket RW-4128 for min_warm_replicas and RW-4129 for per-customer concurrency. linking in follow-up.

dennis: customer message drafted and sent. ACME says they will monitor for 24h and report if anything else. closing loop once postmortem is published.

maria: thanks everyone. please add any missed logs to the RW-incident-1718823456 folder. I'll draft postmortem and link to the change tickets.

sre-bot: Thread closed by maria at 10:16:20 UTC (automated tag).
